title: ANCHOR-FREE: the tree grown from the embeddings alone, no category anchors (one construction, zero LLM calls)
question: Every tree in the record was seeded with the corpus's category labels as depth-1 anchors. Does a tree grown WITHOUT the labels (every train query at the root, the same separation gate proposing k-way splits from depth 0 down) recover the categories, certify structure, and carry capability information, and how does it compare with the same-code anchored control o0 (seed 42, label-free)?

plain_description.what: One tree was grown from the question embeddings alone, without giving it the dataset's category labels as its first layer. It was compared with the same code run with those labels as anchors. No LLM calls were made.
plain_description.why: It tests whether the tree's structure comes from the data or is borrowed from the human category labels it is normally seeded with.
plain_description.information: If the label-free tree recovered the categories and still certified structure, the labels would be doing less work than assumed. Result: done. All three registered criteria passed: purity within 10 points, certified structure, and key information close to the anchored tree's. The labels make cells about 4 to 6 points purer by category (6.4 here, 4.3 on the clean split). The anchors still earn named reporting cells and a little extra key information, so the anchored tree stays the tree of record. The label-free tree has a certified trunk, but a later re-draw cut it to the root plus a 'discursive' branch, about 5 sites. An earlier, stronger reading, that the labels actually cost certifiable structure, was withdrawn.
